cards.title: Server-Side Rendering (SSR)
cards.content:
Angular SSR

By default, Angular runs entirely in the browser (Client-Side Rendering). Server-Side Rendering (SSR) generates the initial HTML on the server before sending it to the client.

This significantly improves First Contentful Paint (FCP) and Search Engine Optimization (SEO).

cards.title: Hydration
cards.content:
Client Hydration

Hydration is the process of restoring the server-rendered HTML into a fully interactive Angular application on the client. Angular 16+ introduced non-destructive hydration via provideClientHydration(), which reuses the existing DOM nodes instead of destroying and recreating them.

cards.title: Adding SSR
cards.content:
Enabling SSR

You can add SSR to an existing Angular project using the CLI:

ng add @angular/ssr

This sets up a Node.js Express server to render your application routes dynamically.

content.prompt: Order the steps of Server-Side Rendering with Hydration.
correctOrder: Server renders Angular app to HTML
Angular client script downloads and hydrates the DOM
